Confirmed on cdk-mintd 0.18.3: a 7-of-7 P2PK swap is accepted, while 8-of-8 and 11-of-11 are rejected with `50000: Proof content too large: 1084 bytes, max 1024` (1483 bytes for eleven signatures).

On the suggested fixes: the mint signs outputs blind and never sees their secrets, so it cannot cap them or reject a lock up front. That leaves the input cap. A lock has up to 11 key slots (`data` plus ten `pubkeys`/`refund` keys, per NUT-28), so the largest valid legacy witness is eleven signatures for P2PK, or ten plus a preimage for HTLC. Raising the witness cap to 2048 for pre-v3 keysets would cover every valid NUT-11/14 witness.

Nothing enforces this, but I don't think gating recv() adds a real bound. Bounded tasks only live until admission: once the waiters queue is full they're refused with Busy immediately, otherwise after max_wait. So a flood of them turns into fast refusals rather than a growing set. Only Unbounded signing can accumulate. That only follows a reservation (swap inputs after a bounded verify, melt change after payment), and once its backlog exceeds max_wait, new verifies time out and the inflow stops.

Gating the receive arm would make bounded requests wait in the channel with no deadline (losing the load shedding), and would put keyset/rotation requests behind sign/verify again. The unbounded jobs it would hold back can't be refused anyway, so they'd just sit in the channel instead of the set. Before this PR they sat in handler futures blocked on pipeline.send.
